I’ve farmed these 8 mu in Quzhou for over thirty years, and I know what works here. Last year my wheat made about 950 jin per mu and the maize hit around 1000 jin, so I’m not changing the rotation — winter wheat followed by summer maize on all 8 mu. Cotton pays more some years, but at 55 my back hurts after too much bending, and the wheat-maize system keeps food on the table without hiring pickers. 

For wheat, I’ll rotary till in early October and sow the improved *Shimai* variety. The extension agent says 15 kg of nitrogen per mu is enough, but I’d rather put down 16 kg — basal compound fertilizer at sowing and a urea topdress at jointing. I can’t afford to under-feed and lose yield. I’ll irrigate three times: once before winter, once at jointing, and once at grain filling. For pests, one herbicide spray and two insecticide sprays should cover it.

For the summer maize, I’ll plant *Nongda 372* hybrid right after wheat harvest in mid-June. There’s no time for ploughing between crops — I’ll no-till direct seed and put down compound fertilizer with the seed. Two irrigations are usually enough here if the summer rains cooperate: one at seedling stage and one at big flare. I’ll spray once for weeds and twice for insects. If the weather is normal, I expect about 520 kg per mu.
